subject: Creative Arts
topic_name: Drama elements in playmaking: structure, grouping, and improvisation

source_trace: Playmaking/group improvisation: structure, grouping, shape, climax. Develop short improvised dramas with a beginning, middle and end. Ask who, what, where, when. Tableaux.
lesson_metadata.source_section: Page 40, Grade 7 Term 1 (detailed content, not the page overview table)

learning_objectives: Develop a short improvised drama in a small group, with a clear beginning, middle, and end.
Use the questions who, what, where, and when to build a scene.
Use a tableau (a frozen picture) to focus the action of a scene.

english_content.narration_script: This term, you'll build your own short dramas through group improvisation -- working in groups of two to four, developing scenes with a genuine structure: a beginning, a middle, and an end, rather than random, disconnected action. A great way to start building any improvised scene is asking four simple questions: who are the characters, what is happening, where is it taking place, and when is it happening? Answering these questions together as a group gives your improvisation real shape. As you build a scene, focus on real listening and concentration -- reacting genuinely to what your scene partners do and say, using their reactions to build the drama together, rather than planning everything in advance. Think too about physical relationships in space: how close or far apart characters stand, what levels they're on, and where the audience's focus should land in the picture you're creating. One powerful tool for this is the tableau -- a frozen, still image that captures a key moment, letting the audience really take in an important point in the story before movement continues. Finally, reflection and feedback matter just as much as performing: discussing your own experience, and exploring specific ways to improve, is how you actually get better at group improvisation over time.

'n Uitstekende manier om enige geïmproviseerde toneel te begin bou is om vier eenvoudige vrae te vra: wie is die karakters, wat gebeur, waar vind dit plaas, en wanneer gebeur dit? Een kragtige hulpmiddel hiervoor is die tablo -- 'n bevrore, stille beeld wat 'n sleuteloomblik vaslê, wat die gehoor toelaat om 'n belangrike punt in die storie regtig in te neem voordat beweging voortduur. subject: Creative Arts
topic_name: Music listening: active listening, meter, and describing music

source_trace: Active listening to recorded or live music by clapping, humming or moving along. Listening to performed music and identifying or describing meter (duple, triple, quadruple), instruments used, and the
lesson_metadata.source_section: Page 52, Grade 7 Term 1 Music Topic 2 (detailed content, not the page overview table -- distinct from the sibling Topic 1 'music literacy' content on the same page)

learning_objectives: Actively listen to recorded or live music by clapping, humming, or moving along.
Identify the meter of a piece of music as duple, triple, or quadruple.
Describe the instruments used and the story or mood a piece of music is telling.

english_content.narration_script: Music isn't just something you hear in the background -- this term, you'll practise truly listening to it. Active listening means engaging with music through your whole body: clapping along to the beat, humming the melody, or simply moving as the music moves you, rather than letting it pass by unnoticed. Once you're actively listening, you can start describing what you hear with real musical vocabulary. First, meter: is the music organised in groups of two beats (duple), three beats (triple), or four beats (quadruple)? Try counting along with a piece -- a waltz famously groups in threes, while a march usually groups in twos or fours. Second, listen for the instruments being used -- can you pick out a guitar, a drum, a voice, a violin? Naming what you hear sharpens your ear over time. Finally, think about the story the music is telling. Does it sound sad or happy? Does it make you think of a particular dance, or does it sound like a march? Music often tells a story or creates a mood without using any words at all, and describing that story in your own words is real musical listening -- not just letting sound wash over you, but actively working out what it's communicating.

visual_storyboard.visual_description: A learner clapping along to music, with sound waves grouped visually into sets of two, three, and four beats.
A thought bubble above a listening learner showing a sad face, a happy face, and a dancing figure, representing the 'story' a piece of music can tell.

afrikaans_content.narration_script: Musiek is nie net iets wat jy op die agtergrond hoor nie -- vanjaar sal jy oefen om werklik daarna te luister. Aktiewe luister beteken om met musiek deur jou hele liggaam om te gaan: saam met die slag te klap, die melodie te neurie, of net te beweeg soos die musiek jou beweeg, eerder as om dit ongemerk te laat verbygaan. Sodra jy aktief luister, kan jy begin om wat jy hoor met werklike musiekwoordeskat te beskryf. Eerste, metrum: is die musiek georganiseer in groepe van twee slae (tweeledig), drie slae (drieledig), of vier slae (vierledig)? Probeer saam met 'n stuk tel -- 'n wals groepeer beroemd in drietalle, terwyl 'n mars gewoonlik in tweetalle of viertalle groepeer. Tweede, luister vir die instrumente wat gebruik word -- kan jy 'n kitaar, 'n tromme, 'n stem, 'n viool uitken? Om te noem wat jy hoor skerp jou oor mettertyd. Laastens, dink aan die storie wat die musiek vertel. Klink dit hartseer of gelukkig? Laat dit jou aan 'n spesifieke dans dink, of klink dit soos 'n mars? Musiek vertel dikwels 'n storie of skep 'n gemoed sonder om enige woorde te gebruik, en om daardie storie in jou eie woorde te beskryf is ware musiekluister -- nie net om klank oor jou te laat spoel nie, maar om aktief uit te werk wat dit kommunikeer.

visual_storyboard.visual_description: 'n Leerder wat saam met musiek klap, met klankgolwe visueel gegroepeer in stelle van twee, drie, en vier slae.
'n Gedagtebel bo 'n luisterende leerder wat 'n hartseer gesig, 'n gelukkige gesig, en 'n dansende figuur wys, wat die 'storie' voorstel wat 'n musiekstuk kan vertel.

worked_example.problem: A song has a strong beat pattern of ONE-two-three, ONE-two-three, repeating. What meter is this?
worked_example.problem_af: 'n Liedjie het 'n sterk slagpatroon van EEN-twee-drie, EEN-twee-drie, wat herhaal. Watter metrum is dit?
solution_steps: Count how many beats repeat in each group.
The pattern groups into sets of three beats.
Three beats per group is triple meter.
worked_example.final_answer: Triple meter (like a waltz).

subject: Creative Arts
topic_name: Performing and creating music: breathing, singing repertoire, and body percussion

source_trace: Breathing exercises. In-tune singing repertoire: folksongs, light music, rounds, part singing. Accompanying songs with body percussion, found/self-made/traditional/Orff instruments. African drumming.

learning_objectives: Use breathing exercises to support in-tune singing.
Perform a folksong, round, or piece of part singing as part of a repertoire.
Accompany a song using body percussion or a found, self-made, or traditional instrument.

english_content.narration_script: Performing and creating music starts with the most basic instrument of all: your own breath. Breathing exercises train you to support your voice properly, which is the foundation for genuinely in-tune singing. This term, you'll build a real repertoire -- a collection of songs you can perform -- including folksongs (indigenous and cultural songs from South Africa and elsewhere), light music, rounds (where different groups sing the same melody starting at different times, overlapping), and part singing, like descants, where different voices sing different but complementary lines at once. As you perform, you'll also accompany songs using body percussion -- clapping, patting, stamping -- or found instruments, self-made instruments, traditional instruments, or Orff instruments (simple pitched percussion instruments common in music classrooms). This term also introduces African drumming and encourages performing music using non-conventional notation, like graphic scores, which use pictures or shapes instead of standard notes. Finally, you'll start creating your own music -- melodic repetition, melodic question-and-answer, and rhythmic improvisation on African drums -- moving from performing other people's music to genuinely making your own.

afrikaans_content.narration_script: Om musiek te vertolk en te skep begin met die mees basiese instrument van almal: jou eie asem. Asemhalingsoefeninge oefen jou om jou stem behoorlik te ondersteun, wat die grondslag is vir werklik suiwer sang. Vanjaar sal jy 'n regte repertoire bou -- 'n versameling liedjies wat jy kan uitvoer -- insluitend volksliedjies (inheemse en kulturele liedjies van Suid-Afrika en elders), ligte musiek, kanons (waar verskillende groepe dieselfde melodie op verskillende tye begin sing, wat oorvleuel), en meerstemmige sang, soos deskante, waar verskillende stemme verskillende maar aanvullende lyne gelyktydig sing. Terwyl jy uitvoer, sal jy ook liedjies begelei met liggaampersoosie -- klap, klop, stamp -- of gevonde instrumente, selfgemaakte instrumente, tradisionele instrumente, of Orff-instrumente (eenvoudige toonhoogte-slaginstrumente algemeen in musieklokale). Vanjaar stel ook Afrika-trommelspel bekend en moedig die uitvoering van musiek met onkonvensionele notasie aan, soos grafiese partiture, wat prente of vorms in plaas van standaardnote gebruik. Laastens sal jy jou eie musiek begin skep -- melodiese herhaling, melodiese vraag-en-antwoord, en ritmiese improvisasie op Afrika-tromme -- deur te beweeg van die uitvoering van ander se musiek na die werklike maak van jou eie.

subject: Creative Arts
topic_name: Dance theory and literacy: terminology, spotting, and cooling-down

source_trace: Dance terminology; Importance of spotting during turning movements; Importance of cooling-down; Talking about own and others' dance work with sensitivity; Discussion of elements of dance: energy/force
lesson_metadata.source_section: Page 29, Grade 7 Term 2 (integrated with Topics 1-2, detailed content, not the page overview table)

learning_objectives: Explain why 'spotting' matters during turning movements, and why cooling-down matters after dancing.
Discuss the dance elements of energy/force and relationships using proper dance vocabulary.
Give feedback on your own and others' dance work with sensitivity and respect.

english_content.narration_script: This term's dance theory builds directly on your practical dance and improvisation classes. First, spotting: when you turn, your head should whip around faster than your body, focusing your eyes on a fixed point each time you face forward again -- this technique, called spotting, prevents dizziness and keeps your turns controlled and safe. Second, cooling-down: just as warming up prepares your body for movement, cooling down afterward -- through relaxation and slow stretching -- helps your muscles recover and reduces soreness. Third, this term introduces giving feedback on dance work with real sensitivity: describing what you noticed in your own or a classmate's performance honestly, but kindly, focusing on specific observations rather than harsh judgments. Finally, you'll discuss two more elements of dance: energy or force (the flow of movement -- is it strong or light, jerky or smooth?), and relationships (how a dancer relates to the floor, to other dancers, or to props). Noticing and naming these qualities in a dance -- your own or someone else's -- is exactly what dance theory and literacy means in practice.

afrikaans_content.narration_script: Vanjaar se dansteorie bou direk op jou praktiese dans- en improvisasieklasse. Eerste, spotting: wanneer jy draai, behoort jou kop vinniger as jou liggaam om te swaai, en jou oë op 'n vaste punt te fokus elke keer as jy weer vorentoe kyk -- hierdie tegniek, genoem spotting, voorkom duiseligheid en hou jou draaie beheer en veilig. Tweede, afkoeling: net soos opwarming jou liggaam voorberei vir beweging, help afkoeling daarna -- deur ontspanning en stadige rek -- jou spiere herstel en verminder stywigheid. Derde, vanjaar stel dit die gee van terugvoer oor danswerk met ware sensitiwiteit bekend: om te beskryf wat jy in jou eie of 'n klasmaat se uitvoering opgemerk het, eerlik maar vriendelik, met fokus op spesifieke waarnemings eerder as harde oordele. Laastens sal jy nog twee elemente van dans bespreek: energie of krag (die vloei van beweging -- is dit sterk of lig, hortend of glad?), en verhoudings (hoe 'n danser met die vloer, ander dansers, of rekwisiete verwant is). Om hierdie eienskappe in 'n dans -- jou eie of iemand anders s'n -- raak te sien en te noem, is presies wat dansteorie en -geletterdheid in die praktyk beteken.

subject: Creative Arts
topic_name: Visual literacy: describing still life using art elements and design principles

source_trace: Art elements (line, tone, texture, shape, colour) and design principles (balance, proportion, harmony, emphasis, contrast) used to describe still life artworks; interpreting symbolic language; express
lesson_metadata.source_section: Page 70, Grade 7 Term 2 Visual Arts Topic 3 (detailed content, not the page overview table)

learning_objectives: Use art elements (line, tone, texture, shape, colour) to describe a still life artwork.
Use design principles (balance, proportion, harmony, emphasis, contrast) to describe how a still life artwork is put together.
Interpret symbolic meaning in a still life artwork and express your own response to it.

english_content.narration_script: Visual literacy means being able to 'read' an artwork the way you'd read a sentence -- noticing its parts and understanding what they add up to. This term, you'll practise this using still life paintings -- artworks showing arranged objects like fruit, bottles, or flowers. Start with art elements: line (edges and outlines), tone (how light or dark an area is), texture (how a surface looks like it would feel), shape, and colour. Naming these in a specific painting -- 'the light falls from the left, creating strong tonal contrast on the fruit' -- is far more precise than just saying 'it looks nice.' Next, design principles describe how those elements are arranged: balance (is the composition even or lopsided?), proportion (are objects sized realistically relative to each other?), harmony (do the colours and shapes feel unified?), emphasis (where does your eye go first?), and contrast (what stands out against what?). Beyond just naming these, visual literacy also means interpreting symbolic language -- a wilting flower might symbolise time passing, for example -- and expressing your own genuine response: what do you notice, what questions does the painting raise for you, and what does it make you think or feel? Looking, talking, listening, and writing about art are all part of becoming visually literate.

afrikaans_content.narration_script: Visuele geletterdheid beteken om 'n kunswerk te kan 'lees' soos jy 'n sin sou lees -- om die dele daarvan raak te sien en te verstaan wat hulle saam beteken. Vanjaar sal jy dit oefen met stillewe-skilderye -- kunswerke wat gerangskikte voorwerpe soos vrugte, bottels, of blomme wys. Begin met kunselemente: lyn (rande en buitelyne), toon (hoe lig of donker 'n area is), tekstuur (hoe 'n oppervlak lyk asof dit sou voel), vorm, en kleur. Om hierdie in 'n spesifieke skildery te noem -- 'die lig val van links, wat sterk toonkontras op die vrugte skep' -- is baie presieser as net te sê 'dit lyk mooi.' Vervolgens beskryf ontwerpbeginsels hoe daardie elemente gerangskik is: balans (is die komposisie eweredig of skeef?), proporsie (is voorwerpe realisties in grootte relatief tot mekaar?), harmonie (voel die kleure en vorms verenig?), klem (waarheen gaan jou oog eerste?), en kontras (wat staan uit teen wat?). Buiten net om hierdie te noem, beteken visuele geletterdheid ook om simboliese taal te interpreteer -- 'n verwelkende blom mag byvoorbeeld tyd wat verbygaan simboliseer -- en om jou eie ware respons uit te druk: wat merk jy op, watter vrae laat die skildery by jou ontstaan, en wat laat dit jou dink of voel? Om na kuns te kyk, daaroor te praat, te luister, en te skryf is almal deel van om visueel geletterd te word.

subject: Creative Arts
topic_name: Performing and creating music: repertoire, accompaniment, and African drumming

source_trace: Breathing exercises. In-tune singing repertoire: folksongs, light music, rounds, part singing (descants). Accompanying songs with body percussion, found/self-made/traditional/Orff instruments. Graphic
lesson_metadata.source_section: Page 54, Grade 7 Term 2 Music Topic 3 (detailed content, not the page overview table)

learning_objectives: Continue developing in-tune singing through a repertoire including folksongs, light music, rounds, and part singing.
Accompany a song using body percussion or a found, self-made, traditional, or Orff instrument.
Create your own short vocal or instrumental music using melodic repetition, question-and-answer, or rhythmic improvisation on African drums.

english_content.narration_script: This term continues building your performing and creating skills, adding new layers of complexity to what you started in Term 1. Breathing exercises remain the foundation, supporting genuinely in-tune singing. Your repertoire grows to include part singing -- songs with descants, where a second voice sings a higher, complementary melody above the main tune, alongside folksongs, light music, and rounds. As you perform, you'll accompany songs using body percussion, or found, self-made, traditional, or Orff instruments -- including instruments you're personally studying. This term also introduces performing and composing music using non-conventional notation, like graphic scores, where pictures or shapes represent sound instead of standard notes -- letting you 'compose' music without needing to read traditional notation at all. African drumming continues to develop, and now you'll start genuinely creating your own music: melodic repetition (repeating a short musical idea, vocally or on an instrument), melodic question-and-answer (one phrase 'asks a question,' and another 'answers' it), and rhythmic improvisation on African drums, where you spontaneously create rhythm patterns rather than following a fixed pattern. Together, these skills move you from simply performing music that already exists toward genuinely making music of your own.

Jou repertoire groei om meerstemmige sang in te sluit -- liedjies met deskante, waar 'n tweede stem 'n hoër, aanvullende melodie bo die hooftoon sing, saam met volksliedjies, ligte musiek, en kanons. Terwyl jy uitvoer, sal jy liedjies begelei met liggaampersoosie, of gevonde, selfgemaakte, tradisionele, of Orff-instrumente -- insluitend instrumente wat jy persoonlik bestudeer. Vanjaar stel dit ook die uitvoering en komposisie van musiek met onkonvensionele notasie bekend, soos grafiese partiture, waar prente of vorms klank verteenwoordig in plaas van standaardnote -- wat jou toelaat om musiek te 'komponeer' sonder om enigsins tradisionele notasie te hoef lees. Afrika-trommelspel ontwikkel voort, en nou sal jy werklik jou eie musiek begin skep: melodiese herhaling (om 'n kort musikale idee te herhaal, vokaal of op 'n instrument), melodiese vraag-en-antwoord (een frase 'vra 'n vraag,' en 'n ander 'antwoord' dit), en ritmiese improvisasie op Afrika-tromme, waar jy spontaan ritmepatrone skep eerder as om 'n vaste patroon te volg. Saam beweeg hierdie vaardighede jou van bloot om musiek uit te voer wat reeds bestaan na werklik om jou eie musiek te maak.

subject: Creative Arts
topic_name: Careers: the creative team behind a production

source_trace: Explore the creative team, including the writer, director, producer, designer, composer, and lighting designer.
lesson_metadata.source_section: Page 41, Grade 7 Term 2 Drama Topic 5 (detailed content, not the page overview table)

learning_objectives: Name the roles that make up a production's 'creative team'.
Explain what the writer, director, and producer of a production each actually do.
Explain what a designer, composer, and lighting designer each contribute to a production.

english_content.narration_script: Every play, film, or show you watch is the result of a whole creative team working together, not just the actors you see on stage or screen. This term's careers focus introduces you to that team. The writer creates the story, characters, and dialogue that everything else is built on. The director shapes how the story is told -- guiding actors, deciding pacing, and creating the overall vision for the production. The producer manages the practical and financial side, making sure the production actually happens -- organising budgets, schedules, and resources. Beyond these three, the designer creates the visual world of the production -- sets, costumes, or props that establish time, place, and mood. The composer writes original music for the production, shaping its emotional tone. And the lighting designer uses light itself as a storytelling tool -- a spotlight, a shift to blue light, or sudden darkness can completely change how an audience feels about a scene. None of these roles work in isolation: a production only comes together when the writer's story, the director's vision, the producer's organisation, and the designer's, composer's, and lighting designer's creative choices all combine into a single, coherent experience.

visual_storyboard.visual_description: Six labelled roles arranged around a central stage: writer, director, producer, designer, composer, lighting designer.
visual_storyboard.on_screen_text: The creative team: six roles behind every production

afrikaans_content.narration_script: Elke toneelstuk, film, of vertoning wat jy kyk is die resultaat van 'n hele kreatiewe span wat saamwerk, nie net die akteurs wat jy op verhoog of skerm sien nie. Vanjaar se loopbaanfokus stel jou aan daardie span voor. Die skrywer skep die storie, karakters, en dialoog waarop alles anders gebou word. Die regisseur vorm hoe die storie vertel word -- lei akteurs, besluit oor tempo, en skep die algehele visie vir die produksie. Die vervaardiger bestuur die praktiese en finansiële kant, en verseker dat die produksie werklik plaasvind -- organiseer begrotings, skedules, en hulpbronne. Buiten hierdie drie, skep die ontwerper die visuele wêreld van die produksie -- stelle, kostuums, of rekwisiete wat tyd, plek, en gemoed vestig. Die komponis skryf oorspronklike musiek vir die produksie, wat sy emosionele toon vorm. En die beligtingsontwerper gebruik lig self as 'n vertelmiddel -- 'n kollig, 'n skuif na blou lig, of skielike donkerte kan heeltemal verander hoe 'n gehoor oor 'n toneel voel. Geeneen van hierdie rolle werk in isolasie nie: 'n produksie kom net saam wanneer die skrywer se storie, die regisseur se visie, die vervaardiger se organisasie, en die ontwerper, komponis, en beligtingsontwerper se kreatiewe keuses almal in 'n enkele, samehangende ervaring saamsmelt.

visual_storyboard.visual_description: Ses geëtiketteerde rolle gerangskik rondom 'n sentrale verhoog: skrywer, regisseur, vervaardiger, ontwerper, komponis, beligtingsontwerper.

subject: Creative Arts
topic_name: Music listening: describing meter, tempo, dynamics, and lyrics

source_trace: Active listening to recorded or live music by clapping, humming or moving along. Following simple musical scores while listening. Describing meter (duple, triple, quadruple), tempo (fast/slow), dynami
lesson_metadata.source_section: Page 53, Grade 7 Term 2 Music Topic 2 (detailed content, not the page overview table -- distinct from the sibling Topic 1 'music literacy' content on the same page)

learning_objectives: Follow a simple musical score while actively listening to a piece of music.
Describe a piece of music's meter, tempo, and dynamics using correct vocabulary.
Describe the meaning, story, or lyrics of a piece of music.

english_content.narration_script: This term adds new layers to your music listening skills, moving beyond just identifying meter into describing music with real precision. As before, active listening means clapping, humming, or moving along with recorded or live music -- but now you'll also try following a simple musical score while you listen, tracking where the music is in the piece as it plays. When describing what you hear, you now have more vocabulary to reach for. Tempo describes speed: is the music fast or slow, and does it speed up or slow down as it goes? Dynamics describes volume: is it soft or loud, and does it grow louder or softer? Combined with meter -- duple, triple, or quadruple -- these give you a genuinely detailed way to describe any piece of music you hear. You'll also keep describing the meaning or story the music tells, and now specifically the lyrics too -- what the words of a song are actually saying, and how they connect to the music's mood. Put together, tempo, dynamics, meter, story, and lyrics let you describe a piece of music almost like describing a scene in a book: not just 'I like this song,' but a genuinely detailed account of exactly what's happening in the sound.

visual_storyboard.visual_description: A learner following a simple musical score with their finger while music plays, alongside a tempo dial showing 'slow' to 'fast'.
A volume dial showing 'soft' to 'loud' (dynamics), next to a speech bubble containing song lyrics.

afrikaans_content.narration_script: Vanjaar voeg nuwe lae by jou musiekluistervaardighede, en beweeg verder as net om metrum te identifiseer na om musiek met ware presisie te beskryf. Soos voorheen beteken aktiewe luister om saam met opgeneemde of lewendige musiek te klap, te neurie, of te beweeg -- maar nou sal jy ook probeer om 'n eenvoudige musiekpartituur te volg terwyl jy luister, en dophou waar die musiek in die stuk is terwyl dit speel. Wanneer jy beskryf wat jy hoor, het jy nou meer woordeskat om na te gryp. Tempo beskryf spoed: is die musiek vinnig of stadig, en versnel of vertraag dit terwyl dit voortgaan? Dinamiek beskryf volume: is dit sag of hard, en word dit harder of sagter? Saam met metrum -- tweeledig, drieledig, of vierledig -- gee dit jou 'n werklik gedetailleerde manier om enige musiekstuk wat jy hoor te beskryf. Jy sal ook aanhou om die betekenis of storie wat die musiek vertel te beskryf, en nou spesifiek ook die lirieke -- wat die woorde van 'n liedjie werklik sê, en hoe dit met die musiek se gemoed verband hou. Saamgevoeg laat tempo, dinamiek, metrum, storie, en lirieke jou toe om 'n musiekstuk amper soos 'n toneel in 'n boek te beskryf: nie net 'ek hou van hierdie liedjie nie,' maar 'n werklik gedetailleerde weergawe van presies wat in die klank gebeur.

subject: Creative Arts
topic_name: Dance improvisation: responding to stimuli, eye contact, and eye focus

source_trace: Response to different stimuli: themes, ideas, stories, pictures, music or props to develop movement vocabulary, utilising knowledge of elements of dance. Exploration of the importance of eye contact a
lesson_metadata.source_section: Page 30, Grade 7 Term 3 (detailed content, not the page overview table)

learning_objectives: Respond to a stimulus (theme, picture, story, music, or prop) by improvising movement.
Use knowledge of the elements of dance to build a personal movement vocabulary from a stimulus.
Explain why eye contact and eye focus matter in a dance performance.

english_content.narration_script: This term's improvisation work starts from stimuli -- an outside idea that sparks your movement, rather than movement that comes from nowhere. A stimulus could be a theme or idea, a story, a picture, a piece of music, or even a physical prop. Your task is to respond to that stimulus by improvising movement, drawing on everything you already know about the elements of dance -- space, time, energy, and relationships -- to build your own personal 'movement vocabulary' in reaction to it. For example, a stimulus like 'a storm' might inspire sudden, sharp, forceful movements, while 'a quiet morning' might inspire slow, gentle, flowing ones. This term also focuses specifically on eye contact and eye focus -- where a dancer chooses to look while performing. A dancer who looks at the floor the whole time seems disconnected and unsure, while deliberate eye focus -- toward the audience, toward a scene partner, or toward a specific point in space -- makes movement feel intentional and confident. Eye focus can even help tell the story of a dance: looking upward might suggest hope or dreaming, looking down might suggest sadness or introspection. Combining a genuine response to a stimulus with confident eye focus is what turns simple movement into real, expressive dance improvisation.

afrikaans_content.narration_script: Vanjaar se improvisasiewerk begin by stimuli -- 'n buite-idee wat jou beweging aan die gang sit, eerder as beweging wat uit die niet kom. 'n Stimulus mag 'n tema of idee, 'n storie, 'n prentjie, 'n musiekstuk, of selfs 'n fisiese rekwisiet wees. Jou taak is om op daardie stimulus te reageer deur beweging te improviseer, en te put uit alles wat jy reeds oor die elemente van dans weet -- ruimte, tyd, energie, en verhoudings -- om jou eie persoonlike 'bewegingswoordeskat' in reaksie daarop te bou. Byvoorbeeld, 'n stimulus soos 'n storm' mag skielike, skerp, kragtige bewegings inspireer, terwyl 'n stil oggend' stadige, sagte, vloeiende bewegings mag inspireer. Vanjaar fokus ook spesifiek op oogkontak en oogfokus -- waar 'n danser kies om te kyk terwyl hulle optree. 'n Danser wat die hele tyd na die vloer kyk lyk ontkoppel en onseker, terwyl doelbewuste oogfokus -- na die gehoor, na 'n tonelemaat, of na 'n spesifieke punt in die ruimte -- beweging doelbewus en selfversekerd laat voel. Oogfokus kan selfs help om die storie van 'n dans te vertel: om opwaarts te kyk mag hoop of droom voorstel, om af te kyk mag hartseer of selfondersoek voorstel. Om 'n ware reaksie op 'n stimulus met selfversekerde oogfokus te kombineer is wat eenvoudige beweging in werklike, uitdrukkende dansimprovisasie verander.

subject: Creative Arts
topic_name: Dance theory and literacy: how movement conveys meaning, comparing dance forms

source_trace: Discussion of how movements may convey meaning. Selection of three different dance forms, viewing excerpts on DVD/live and discussion of their similarities and differences.
lesson_metadata.source_section: Page 30, Grade 7 Term 3 (integrated with Topics 1-2, detailed content, not the page overview table)

learning_objectives: Explain how a specific movement or gesture can convey meaning in a dance.
Watch excerpts from three different dance forms and identify at least one similarity between them.
Identify at least one difference between three different dance forms.

english_content.narration_script: Dance theory this term asks a big question: how does movement actually mean something? A raised arm, a collapsing body, a sudden freeze -- each of these physical actions can communicate an idea or emotion just as clearly as words can, if you know how to read them. A slow, sinking movement might convey sadness or defeat; a sharp, explosive movement might convey anger or excitement; a wide, open gesture might convey welcome or joy. Learning to notice this is a core skill of dance literacy. This term, you'll also watch excerpts from three different dance forms -- these might include, for example, ballet, traditional South African dance, and contemporary dance -- either live or on video. As you watch, look for similarities: perhaps all three use repetition, or all three respond to rhythm in music. Then look for differences: the forms might differ in their use of space, their level of formality, the stories they tell, or the parts of the body they emphasise most. Comparing dance forms this way sharpens your understanding of what makes each style unique, while also revealing what all dance, across cultures and styles, actually shares in common: the ability to use the human body to communicate something that words alone cannot.

afrikaans_content.narration_script: Dansteorie vra vanjaar 'n groot vraag: hoe beteken beweging eintlik iets? 'n Opgeligte arm, 'n insakkende liggaam, 'n skielike vries -- elkeen van hierdie fisiese aksies kan 'n idee of emosie net so duidelik as woorde kommunikeer, as jy weet hoe om dit te lees. 'n Stadige, sinkende beweging mag hartseer of nederlaag voorstel; 'n skerp, ontploffende beweging mag woede of opgewondenheid voorstel; 'n wye, oop gebaar mag welkom of vreugde voorstel. Om dit te leer raaksien is 'n kernvaardigheid van dansgeletterdheid. Vanjaar sal jy ook uittreksels van drie verskillende dansvorme kyk -- dit mag byvoorbeeld ballet, tradisionele Suid-Afrikaanse dans, en kontemporêre dans insluit -- lewendig of op video. Terwyl jy kyk, soek na ooreenkomste: dalk gebruik al drie herhaling, of al drie reageer op ritme in musiek. Soek dan na verskille: die vorme mag verskil in hul gebruik van ruimte, hul vlak van formaliteit, die stories wat hulle vertel, of die liggaamsdele wat hulle die meeste beklemtoon. Om dansvorme so te vergelyk skerp jou begrip van wat elke styl uniek maak, terwyl dit ook openbaar wat alle dans, regoor kulture en style, eintlik gemeen het: die vermoë om die menslike liggaam te gebruik om iets te kommunikeer wat woorde alleen nie kan nie.

subject: Creative Arts
topic_name: Drama elements in playmaking: character, and drama elements in cultural and social events

source_trace: Character observation, imitation and imagination in short improvised dramas (groups of 2-4): listening and concentration, action and reaction, characterisation (voice, body, relationships, environment
lesson_metadata.source_section: Page 42, Grade 7 Term 3 Drama Topic 2 (detailed content, not the page overview table)

learning_objectives: Build a short improvised drama in a small group using genuine listening, concentration, and reaction.
Make clear character choices using voice and body, and understand relationships between characters.
Identify the drama elements (actors, audience, space, time, costumes, props, and more) present in a cultural or social event.

english_content.narration_script: This term deepens your playmaking skills in two directions. First, character work: in groups of two to four, you'll build short improvised dramas grounded in real listening and concentration -- genuinely reacting to what your scene partners do and say, rather than planning your own lines in advance. Characterisation means making clear choices: how does your character's voice sound, how does their body move, and how do they relate to the other characters and to the environment they're in? A confident character might stand tall and speak firmly; a nervous character might fidget and speak quietly -- these choices, made clearly and consistently, are what make a character believable. Second, this term looks at drama elements in cultural and social events -- like a wedding ceremony or an opening ceremony -- comparing them directly to theatre. Both share the same underlying elements: actors (the people with roles to play), an audience (people watching or participating), space (how the area is arranged), time (specific timing and duration), costumes, props, special effects, music or accompaniment, movement or choreography, and chants or call-and-response. Recognising these same elements in a real cultural event as you would in a play reveals something important: performance and ceremony aren't as different as they might first seem -- both are carefully structured experiences designed to have an impact on the people present.

afrikaans_content.narration_script: Vanjaar verdiep jou speltoneelmaak-vaardighede in twee rigtings. Eerste, karakterwerk: in groepe van twee tot vier, sal jy kort geïmproviseerde dramas bou gegrond op ware luister en konsentrasie -- werklik reageer op wat jou tonelemaats doen en sê, eerder as om jou eie lyne vooraf te beplan. Karakterisering beteken om duidelike keuses te maak: hoe klink jou karakter se stem, hoe beweeg hul liggaam, en hoe verwant hulle aan die ander karakters en aan die omgewing waarin hulle is? 'n Selfversekerde karakter mag regop staan en ferm praat; 'n senuweeagtige karakter mag lastig wees en sag praat -- hierdie keuses, duidelik en konsekwent gemaak, is wat 'n karakter geloofwaardig maak. Tweede, vanjaar kyk na dramaelemente in kulturele en sosiale gebeure -- soos 'n troueseremonie of 'n openingseremonie -- en vergelyk hulle direk met teater. Beide deel dieselfde onderliggende elemente: akteurs (die mense met rolle om te speel), 'n gehoor (mense wat kyk of deelneem), ruimte (hoe die area gerangskik is), tyd (spesifieke tydsberekening en duur), kostuums, rekwisiete, spesiale effekte, musiek of begeleiding, beweging of choreografie, en gesange of oproep-en-antwoord. Om hierdie selfde elemente in 'n werklike kulturele gebeurtenis raak te sien soos jy in 'n toneelstuk sou, openbaar iets belangriks: uitvoering en seremonie is nie so verskillend as wat hulle aanvanklik mag lyk nie -- beide is sorgvuldig gestruktureerde ervarings ontwerp om 'n impak op die mense teenwoordig te hê.

subject: Creative Arts
topic_name: Careers: the support team behind a production

source_trace: Explore the support team, including the stage manager, stage hands, make-up artists, costume mistress, props mistress, lighting and sound technicians and front of house staff.
lesson_metadata.source_section: Page 42, Grade 7 Term 3 Drama Topic 5 (detailed content, not the page overview table)

learning_objectives: Name at least four support-team roles behind a theatre production.
Explain what a stage manager and stage hands actually do during a production.
Explain what front of house staff do, and why their role matters even though they're not on stage.

english_content.narration_script: Last term you met the creative team; this term you'll meet the support team -- the people who make sure a production actually runs smoothly, night after night, often without the audience ever noticing them. The stage manager is the operational heart of a production, coordinating everything backstage and calling cues during the actual show. Stage hands move sets, props, and equipment during scene changes, often working quickly in the dark between scenes. Make-up artists and the costume mistress transform actors into their characters -- applying make-up and creating, fitting, and maintaining costumes. The props mistress manages every object used on stage, making sure the right prop is in the right place at the right time. Lighting and sound technicians operate the actual equipment, executing the choices the lighting designer and composer made during rehearsals. Finally, front of house staff -- ushers, ticket sellers, programme sellers -- manage the audience's experience before the show even starts and during interval, even though they never appear on stage at all. What connects all these roles is this: a production isn't just what happens in the spotlight -- it's dozens of coordinated, often invisible jobs, and if any one of them fails, the audience notices immediately, even if they can't say exactly why.

afrikaans_content.narration_script: Verlede kwartaal het jy die kreatiewe span ontmoet; vanjaar sal jy die ondersteuningspan ontmoet -- die mense wat verseker dat 'n produksie werklik glad verloop, aand na aand, dikwels sonder dat die gehoor hulle ooit opmerk. Die verhoogbestuurder is die operasionele hart van 'n produksie, koördineer alles agter die skerms en roep leidrade tydens die werklike vertoning. Verhoogwerkers beweeg stelle, rekwisiete, en toerusting tydens toneelveranderinge, en werk dikwels vinnig in die donker tussen tonele. Grimeerkunstenaars en die kostuummeesteres verander akteurs in hul karakters -- pas grimering toe en skep, pas, en onderhou kostuums. Die rekwisietemeesteres bestuur elke voorwerp wat op die verhoog gebruik word, en verseker dat die regte rekwisiet op die regte plek op die regte tyd is. Beligtings- en klanktegnici bedryf die werklike toerusting, en voer die keuses uit wat die beligtingsontwerper en komponis tydens repetisies gemaak het. Laastens bestuur voorhuis-personeel -- plekaanwysers, kaartjieverkopers, programverkopers -- die gehoor se ervaring voordat die vertoning selfs begin en tydens pouse, alhoewel hulle nooit op die verhoog verskyn nie. Wat al hierdie rolle verbind is dit: 'n produksie is nie net wat in die kollig gebeur nie -- dit is tientalle gekoördineerde, dikwels onsigbare werke, en as enige een van hulle faal, merk die gehoor dit onmiddellik op, al kan hulle nie presies sê hoekom nie.

subject: Creative Arts
topic_name: Music listening: texture and creating a graphic score

source_trace: Active listening to recorded or live music by clapping, humming or moving along. Describing meter, tempo, dynamics, meaning/story, lyrics, and texture of the music. Creating a graphic score (sound pic
lesson_metadata.source_section: Page 55, Grade 7 Term 3 Music Topic 2 (detailed content, not the page overview table -- distinct from the sibling Topic 1 'music literacy' and Topic 3 'Performing and Creating' content on the same page)

learning_objectives: Describe the texture of a piece of music, alongside its meter, tempo, and dynamics.
Continue active listening skills by clapping, humming, or moving along to a piece of music.
Create a graphic score (a sound picture) representing a piece of music you have listened to.

english_content.narration_script: This term adds one final, rich layer to your music listening vocabulary: texture. Texture describes how many musical layers are happening at once, and how they relate -- is it just one single melody (thin texture), or many instruments and voices layered together (thick texture)? Learning to hear texture, alongside the meter, tempo, dynamics, story, and lyrics you've already studied, gives you an almost complete toolkit for describing any piece of music in real depth. This term's biggest new skill, though, is creating your own graphic score -- a 'sound picture' that represents music visually, using shapes, lines, colours, or symbols instead of standard notation. Imagine listening to a recording of a storm: you might draw jagged, dark lines for the thunder, soft wavy lines for gentle rain, and a sudden burst of colour for a lightning crack. There's no single 'correct' way to draw a graphic score -- what matters is that your picture genuinely captures what you heard: the loud parts and quiet parts, the fast moments and slow ones, the thick, busy sections and the thin, sparse ones. Creating a graphic score is a brilliant way to prove you're really listening -- because you can't draw a convincing sound picture of music you weren't paying attention to.

visual_storyboard.visual_description: Two side-by-side music visualisations: one thin single wavy line (thin texture) and one with many overlapping layered lines (thick texture).
visual_storyboard.on_screen_text: Texture: thin (one layer) versus thick (many layers)

visual_storyboard.on_screen_text: Creating a graphic score: a 'sound picture' of music

afrikaans_content.narration_script: Vanjaar voeg een finale, ryk laag by jou musiekluisterwoordeskat: tekstuur. Tekstuur beskryf hoeveel musikale lae gelyktydig gebeur, en hoe hulle verband hou -- is dit net een enkele melodie (dun tekstuur), of baie instrumente en stemme saam gelaag (dik tekstuur)? Om tekstuur te leer hoor, saam met die metrum, tempo, dinamiek, storie, en lirieke wat jy reeds bestudeer het, gee jou 'n amper volledige gereedskapstel om enige musiekstuk in werklike diepte te beskryf. Vanjaar se grootste nuwe vaardigheid is egter om jou eie grafiese partituur te skep -- 'n 'klankprentjie' wat musiek visueel voorstel, met vorms, lyne, kleure, of simbole in plaas van standaardnotasie. Verbeel jou jy luister na 'n opname van 'n storm: jy mag hortende, donker lyne vir die donderweer teken, sagte golwende lyne vir sagte reën, en 'n skielike kleurbars vir 'n weerligflits. Daar is nie 'n enkele 'korrekte' manier om 'n grafiese partituur te teken nie -- wat saak maak is dat jou prentjie werklik vasvang wat jy gehoor het: die harde dele en stil dele, die vinnige oomblikke en stadige, die dik, besige gedeeltes en die dun, spaars gedeeltes. Om 'n grafiese partituur te skep is 'n uitstekende manier om te bewys dat jy werklik luister -- want jy kan nie 'n oortuigende klankprentjie teken van musiek waarop jy nie aandag gegee het nie.

visual_storyboard.visual_description: Twee langs-mekaar musiekvisualiserings: een dun enkele golwende lyn (dun tekstuur) en een met baie oorvleuelende gelaagde lyne (dik tekstuur).
visual_storyboard.on_screen_text: Tekstuur: dun (een laag) teenoor dik (baie lae)

visual_storyboard.visual_description: 'n Leerder wat 'n grafiese partituur van 'n storm teken -- hortende donker lyne vir donderweer, sagte golwende lyne vir reën, en 'n helder bars vir weerlig.

solution_steps: Texture describes how many layers are happening at once.
One instrument playing one melody is a single layer.
A single layer is thin texture.
worked_example.final_answer: Thin texture (just one layer).

practice_questions.correct_answer: How many musical layers are happening at once, and how they relate.
practice_questions.hint_en: Think about the difference between one instrument playing alone versus a full orchestra.
practice_questions.hint_af: Dink aan die verskil tussen een instrument wat alleen speel teenoor 'n volle orkes.

practice_questions.question_en: What is a 'graphic score'?
practice_questions.question_af: Wat is 'n 'grafiese partituur'?
practice_questions.correct_answer: A visual 'sound picture' of music using shapes, lines, colours, or symbols instead of standard notation.
practice_questions.hint_en: Think about drawing what you hear instead of writing standard notes.
practice_questions.hint_af: Dink aan om te teken wat jy hoor in plaas daarvan om standaardnote te skryf.

practice_questions.question_af: Hoekom moet jy noukeurig luister voordat jy 'n grafiese partituur teken?
practice_questions.correct_answer: Because the picture needs to genuinely capture what was heard (loud/quiet, fast/slow, thick/thin) to be convincing.
practice_questions.hint_en: Think about whether you could draw an accurate picture of something you weren't paying attention to.
practice_questions.hint_af: Dink aan of jy 'n akkurate prentjie kan teken van iets waarop jy nie aandag gegee het nie.

subject: Creative Arts
topic_name: Performing and creating music: repertoire, ostinato improvisation, and sound pictures

source_trace: Breathing exercises. In-tune singing repertoire: folksongs, light music, rounds, part singing (descants, soprano/alto, soprano/baritone). Accompaniment with body percussion/instruments. Non-convention
lesson_metadata.source_section: Page 55, Grade 7 Term 3 Music Topic 3 (detailed content, not the page overview table)

learning_objectives: Continue developing in-tune singing through a repertoire including part singing with multiple voice combinations.
Improvise rhythmically or melodically on an ostinato or riff, vocally or on an instrument.
Create a sound picture based on a story or poem using voice or instruments.

english_content.narration_script: Your performing and creating skills reach new depth this term. Your singing repertoire now includes part singing in more combinations -- descants, but also soprano/alto and soprano/baritone pairings, where different voice types sing complementary lines together. You'll keep accompanying songs with body percussion and instruments, and keep performing music using non-conventional notation like graphic scores, alongside continued African drumming. The real leap this term is in creating your own music. You'll practise melodic repetition and melodic question-and-answer as before, but now add improvisation on an ostinato or riff -- a short, repeating musical or rhythmic pattern that stays constant while you improvise new material over the top of it, either rhythmically (by clapping or drumming) or melodically (with your voice or an instrument). Think of the ostinato as a steady foundation, freeing you to experiment on top of it without losing the beat. Finally, you'll create a sound picture based on a story or poem, using your voice or instruments to represent its events and moods in sound -- similar to a graphic score, but built directly from a piece of literature rather than from listening to existing music. Across all of this, the theme is the same: moving from performing what already exists to genuinely composing something of your own.

visual_storyboard.on_screen_text: Part singing: soprano, alto, baritone combinations

afrikaans_content.narration_script: Jou uitvoerings- en skeppingsvaardighede bereik vanjaar nuwe diepte. Jou sangrepertoire sluit nou meerstemmige sang in meer kombinasies in -- deskante, maar ook sopraan/alt en sopraan/bariton-parings, waar verskillende stemtipes aanvullende lyne saam sing. Jy sal aanhou om liedjies met liggaampersoosie en instrumente te begelei, en aanhou om musiek met onkonvensionele notasie soos grafiese partiture uit te voer, saam met voortgesette Afrika-trommelspel. Die werklike sprong vanjaar is in die skep van jou eie musiek. Jy sal melodiese herhaling en melodiese vraag-en-antwoord soos voorheen oefen, maar nou improvisasie op 'n ostinato of riff byvoeg -- 'n kort, herhalende musikale of ritmiese patroon wat konstant bly terwyl jy nuwe materiaal daarbo improviseer, óf ritmies (deur te klap of te trom) óf melodies (met jou stem of 'n instrument). Dink aan die ostinato as 'n stabiele grondslag, wat jou vrylaat om daarbo te eksperimenteer sonder om die slag te verloor. Laastens sal jy 'n klankprentjie skep gebaseer op 'n storie of gedig, deur jou stem of instrumente te gebruik om sy gebeure en gemoede in klank voor te stel -- soortgelyk aan 'n grafiese partituur, maar direk gebou uit 'n stuk literatuur eerder as uit luister na bestaande musiek. Regoor al hierdie is die tema dieselfde: om te beweeg van die uitvoering van wat reeds bestaan na werklik om iets van jou eie te komponeer.

visual_storyboard.on_screen_text: Meerstemmige sang: sopraan, alt, bariton kombinasies

visual_storyboard.visual_description: 'n Herhalende ostinato-ritmepatroon gewys as 'n stabiele lus, met 'n tweede, vrylik geïmproviseerde melodie daarbo gelaag.

worked_example.problem_af: 'n Tromspeler herhaal dieselfde vier-slag ritmepatroon deurlopend terwyl 'n tweede musikant 'n nuwe melodie daaroor improviseer. Wat word die herhalende patroon genoem?
solution_steps: A short, constantly repeating musical or rhythmic pattern is an ostinato (or riff).
It provides a steady foundation for improvisation above it.
worked_example.final_answer: An ostinato (or riff).

practice_questions.question_en: What is an 'ostinato'?
practice_questions.question_af: Wat is 'n 'ostinato'?
practice_questions.correct_answer: A short, repeating musical or rhythmic pattern that stays constant while other material is improvised over it.

subject: Creative Arts
topic_name: Visual literacy: the role of the artist and buildings as heritage

source_trace: Art elements and design principles used to describe artworks (e.g. buildings). The role of the artist in society. Personal expression and interpretation of architecture. Social development: similariti
lesson_metadata.source_section: Page 71, Grade 7 Term 3 Visual Arts Topic 3 (detailed content, not the page overview table)

learning_objectives: Use art elements and design principles to describe a building as a work of visual art.
Explain the role of the artist as a contributor to society.
Explain how buildings and architecture can function as cultural heritage.

english_content.narration_script: This term applies visual literacy to a subject you might not usually think of as 'art': buildings. Using the same art elements and design principles you've used for paintings -- line, shape, texture, balance, proportion, contrast -- you can describe a building's design just as precisely as you'd describe a painting: the strong vertical lines of columns, the balance between window placement, the contrast between rough stone and smooth glass. This term also asks a bigger question: what role does an artist -- or an architect -- actually play in society? An artist isn't just someone who makes decorative objects; they're a contributor to how a society sees itself, expresses its values, and remembers its history. This connects directly to the idea of buildings as heritage: an old building isn't just a structure, it's a physical record of a community's history, values, and identity, carrying meaning across generations. As you interpret architecture personally, you'll also practise social and values development: recognising similarities and differences between how different communities build and design, respecting the arts as heritage, and genuinely respecting other people's opinions and interpretations of a building, even when they differ from your own. Visual literacy, applied to buildings, ultimately teaches the same lesson it always does: looking closely, and talking, listening, and writing about what you see, reveals meaning that a quick glance would miss entirely.

visual_storyboard.visual_description: A building's facade with labelled art elements and design principles -- vertical lines of columns, contrast between stone and glass, balanced window placement.
visual_storyboard.on_screen_text: Reading a building like an artwork: line, contrast, balance

visual_storyboard.visual_description: An old heritage building with a timeline showing generations of a community connected to it, symbolising buildings as cultural memory.

afrikaans_content.narration_script: Vanjaar pas visuele geletterdheid toe op 'n onderwerp wat jy dalk nie gewoonlik as 'kuns' sou beskou nie: geboue. Deur dieselfde kunselemente en ontwerpbeginsels te gebruik wat jy vir skilderye gebruik het -- lyn, vorm, tekstuur, balans, proporsie, kontras -- kan jy 'n gebou se ontwerp net so presies beskryf as wat jy 'n skildery sou beskryf: die sterk vertikale lyne van pilare, die balans tussen vensterplasing, die kontras tussen growwe klip en gladde glas. Vanjaar vra ook 'n groter vraag: watter rol speel 'n kunstenaar -- of 'n argitek -- werklik in die samelewing? 'n Kunstenaar is nie net iemand wat dekoratiewe voorwerpe maak nie; hulle is 'n bydraer tot hoe 'n samelewing homself sien, sy waardes uitdruk, en sy geskiedenis onthou. Dit hou direk verband met die idee van geboue as erfenis: 'n ou gebou is nie net 'n struktuur nie, dit is 'n fisiese rekord van 'n gemeenskap se geskiedenis, waardes, en identiteit, wat betekenis regoor generasies dra. Terwyl jy argitektuur persoonlik interpreteer, sal jy ook sosiale en waardeontwikkeling oefen: om ooreenkomste en verskille tussen hoe verskillende gemeenskappe bou en ontwerp raak te sien, om die kunste as erfenis te respekteer, en om werklik ander mense se menings en interpretasies van 'n gebou te respekteer, selfs wanneer dit van jou eie verskil. Visuele geletterdheid, toegepas op geboue, leer uiteindelik dieselfde les wat dit altyd doen: om noukeurig te kyk, en te praat, te luister, en te skryf oor wat jy sien, openbaar betekenis wat 'n vinnige oogopslag heeltemal sou mis.

visual_storyboard.visual_description: 'n Gebou se fasade met geëtiketteerde kunselemente en ontwerpbeginsels -- vertikale lyne van pilare, kontras tussen klip en glas, gebalanseerde vensterplasing.
visual_storyboard.on_screen_text: Lees 'n gebou soos 'n kunswerk: lyn, kontras, balans

visual_storyboard.visual_description: 'n Ou erfenisgebou met 'n tydlyn wat generasies van 'n gemeenskap daaraan gekoppel wys, wat geboue as kulturele geheue simboliseer.
visual_storyboard.on_screen_text: Geboue as erfenis: 'n fisiese rekord van geskiedenis

worked_example.problem: An old town hall has thick stone walls, small windows, and a symmetrical facade. Using one design principle, explain how its symmetry affects how it looks.
worked_example.problem_af: 'n Ou stadsaal het dik klipmure, klein vensters, en 'n simmetriese fasade. Verduidelik met een ontwerpbeginsel hoe sy simmetrie beïnvloed hoe dit lyk.
solution_steps: A symmetrical facade means both sides mirror each other evenly.
This creates balance, making the building feel stable and orderly.
worked_example.final_answer: The symmetry creates balance, making the building feel stable and orderly.

practice_questions.question_en: Name two art elements or design principles that could describe a building.
practice_questions.question_af: Noem twee kunselemente of ontwerpbeginsels wat 'n gebou kan beskryf.
practice_questions.correct_answer: Any two of: line, shape, texture, balance, proportion, contrast.
practice_questions.hint_en: These are the same tools used to describe a painting.
practice_questions.hint_af: Hierdie is dieselfde gereedskap gebruik om 'n skildery te beskryf.

practice_questions.question_en: In what sense can a building be 'heritage'?
practice_questions.question_af: In watter sin kan 'n gebou 'erfenis' wees?
practice_questions.correct_answer: It can be a physical record of a community's history, values, and identity across generations.
practice_questions.hint_en: Think about what an old building can tell you about the people who built and used it.
practice_questions.hint_af: Dink aan wat 'n ou gebou jou kan vertel oor die mense wat dit gebou en gebruik het.

practice_questions.question_en: Why is respecting other people's interpretations of a building part of this lesson?
practice_questions.question_af: Hoekom is dit om ander mense se interpretasies van 'n gebou te respekteer deel van hierdie les?
practice_questions.correct_answer: Because different people and communities may see different meaning or value in the same building, and values development includes respecting that.
practice_questions.hint_en: Think about two people seeing the same building very differently.
practice_questions.hint_af: Dink aan twee mense wat dieselfde gebou baie verskillend sien.

subject: Creative Arts
topic_name: Create in 3D: pattern-making with recyclable materials

source_trace: Art elements (shape, line, tone, texture, colour) and design principles (proportion, emphasis, contrast) in 3D construction and modelling. Craftsmanship: pasting, cutting, wrapping, tying, stitching.
lesson_metadata.source_section: Page 71, Grade 7 Term 3 Visual Arts Topic 2 (detailed content, not the page overview table)

learning_objectives: Apply art elements and design principles (proportion, emphasis, contrast) to a 3D construction.
Use craftsmanship techniques (pasting, cutting, wrapping, tying, stitching) with recyclable materials.
Create a repeat pattern as surface decoration on a 3D object.

english_content.narration_script: This term moves your art-making from flat, two-dimensional work into three dimensions -- creating real, physical objects you can hold and turn around. Using recyclable materials, fabric off-cuts, beads, coloured cottons, and ribbons, you'll construct something useful, like a holder for a cell phone, CDs, or a candle. The same art elements apply here as in 2D work -- shape, line, tone, texture, colour -- but now you're also thinking about how the object looks from every angle, not just one. Design principles like proportion (does the object feel well-sized in all its parts?), emphasis (what draws the eye first?), and contrast remain just as important in three dimensions as in two. Craftsmanship becomes central this term: pasting, cutting, wrapping, tying, and stitching are the actual physical skills that turn loose materials into a finished object, and getting genuinely good at them takes practice and patience. A major new skill this term is pattern-making -- creating your own repeat patterns as surface decoration, experimenting with how art elements and design principles combine when a shape or motif repeats across a surface. Finally, working with real tools and materials means genuine safety matters: using tools carefully, being considerate of others working nearby, and sharing resources responsibly are just as much a part of this term's learning as the artwork itself.

visual_storyboard.on_screen_text: 3D craft: shape, texture, and proportion from every angle

visual_storyboard.visual_description: A close-up of a repeating pattern being stitched or pasted as surface decoration on the object.

afrikaans_content.narration_script: Vanjaar beweeg jou kunswerk van plat, tweedimensionele werk na drie dimensies -- om werklike, fisiese voorwerpe te skep wat jy kan vashou en omdraai. Deur herwinbare materiale, stofafsnitte, krale, gekleurde garing, en linte te gebruik, sal jy iets nuttigs bou, soos 'n houer vir 'n selfoon, CD's, of 'n kers. Dieselfde kunselemente geld hier soos in 2D-werk -- vorm, lyn, toon, tekstuur, kleur -- maar nou dink jy ook aan hoe die voorwerp van elke hoek af lyk, nie net een nie. Ontwerpbeginsels soos proporsie (voel die voorwerp goed-groot in al sy dele?), klem (wat trek die oog eerste?), en kontras bly net so belangrik in drie dimensies as in twee. Vakmanskap word vanjaar sentraal: plak, sny, toedraai, vasbind, en stik is die werklike fisiese vaardighede wat los materiale in 'n voltooide voorwerp verander, en om werklik goed daarin te word verg oefening en geduld. 'n Groot nuwe vaardigheid vanjaar is patroonmaak -- om jou eie herhalende patrone as oppervlakversiering te skep, en te eksperimenteer met hoe kunselemente en ontwerpbeginsels kombineer wanneer 'n vorm of motief oor 'n oppervlak herhaal. Laastens, om met werklike gereedskap en materiale te werk beteken dat werklike veiligheid saak maak: om gereedskap versigtig te gebruik, ander wat naby werk in ag te neem, en hulpbronne verantwoordelik te deel is net so 'n deel van vanjaar se leer as die kunswerk self.

worked_example.problem: You are building a small holder using recyclable cardboard and beads. Which craftsmanship technique would you use to attach the beads securely?
worked_example.problem_af: Jy bou 'n klein houertjie met herwinbare karton en krale. Watter vakmanskaptegniek sal jy gebruik om die krale veilig vas te maak?
solution_steps: Beads need to be attached securely to a surface.
Stitching or tying are craftsmanship techniques suited to securely attaching small objects like beads.
worked_example.final_answer: Stitching or tying (rather than, for example, just resting them loosely).

practice_questions.question_en: Name two craftsmanship techniques used in 3D construction this term.

topic_name: Dance theory and literacy: revision for formal assessment

source_trace: Revision of dance theory and literacy topics from terms 1, 2 and 3 for formal assessment.
lesson_metadata.source_section: Page 31, Grade 7 Term 4 (integrated with Topics 1-2, detailed content, not the page overview table)

learning_objectives: Recall and explain dance terminology covered across terms 1 to 3.
Recall the elements of dance covered this year: space, time, energy/force, and relationships.
Prepare confidently for a short written test on dance theory and literacy.

english_content.narration_script: This term brings together everything you've learned about dance theory across the whole year, in preparation for a formal written test. Let's revise the key ideas. From Term 1, you learned dance terminology, the importance of warming up, and good posture and alignment, along with the elements of space and time. From Term 2, you added spotting during turns, the importance of cooling down, giving feedback with sensitivity, and the elements of energy/force and relationships. From Term 3, you explored how movement conveys meaning, and compared three different dance forms for their similarities and differences. Together, these four elements of dance -- space, time, energy/force, and relationships -- form the backbone of everything you've studied: any dance you watch or perform can be analysed and described using these four ideas. As you prepare for your test, it helps to practise explaining each idea in your own words, rather than just memorising definitions -- if you can explain why spotting prevents dizziness, or how a slow, sinking movement might convey sadness, you genuinely understand the theory, not just the vocabulary. Revision like this isn't about learning anything new -- it's about pulling a whole year of dance theory into one clear, confident picture in your mind before the test.

Van Kwartaal 1 het jy dansterminologie geleer, die belangrikheid van opwarming, en goeie postuur en belyning, saam met die elemente van ruimte en tyd. Van Kwartaal 2 het jy spotting tydens draaie bygevoeg, die belangrikheid van afkoeling, om terugvoer met sensitiwiteit te gee, en die elemente van energie/krag en verhoudings. source_trace: Explore the related fields of study, including the drama teacher, drama therapist, drama life coach, voice and speech therapist, movement therapist, radio and television presenters, master-of-ceremoni

learning_objectives: Name at least four careers related to drama beyond acting itself.
Explain how drama skills can be used therapeutically, in roles like drama therapist or movement therapist.
Explain how drama skills apply to careers like radio/TV presenting or being a master of ceremonies.

english_content.narration_script: This final term's careers focus looks beyond the stage entirely, to careers where drama skills apply in surprising and valuable ways. A drama teacher shares these skills with others, guiding students the way your own teacher guides you. A drama therapist and a drama life coach use drama techniques -- like role-play, storytelling, and improvisation -- to help people process emotions, build confidence, or work through personal challenges; drama, in these careers, becomes a tool for healing and growth, not performance for an audience. Similarly, a voice and speech therapist helps people who have difficulty speaking or using their voice, drawing on exactly the vocal techniques you've practised all year. A movement therapist uses physical movement -- much like the dance and drama movement work you've done -- to support people's physical or emotional wellbeing. Beyond therapy, drama skills also power careers like radio and television presenting, where clear, engaging vocal delivery and audience connection matter enormously, and being a master of ceremonies, who keeps an event flowing and holds an audience's attention. Finally, agents represent performers professionally, helping them find and manage work. What connects all these careers is this: the skills you've built all year -- vocal expression, movement, characterisation, confidence in front of others -- are valuable far beyond the stage itself.

'n Dramaonderwyser deel hierdie vaardighede met ander, en lei studente soos jou eie onderwyser jou lei. 'n Dramaterapeut en 'n dramalewensafrigter gebruik dramategnieke -- soos rolspel, storievertelling, en improvisasie -- om mense te help om emosies te verwerk, selfvertroue te bou, of persoonlike uitdagings te deurwerk; drama, in hierdie loopbane, word 'n hulpmiddel vir genesing en groei, nie vertoning vir 'n gehoor nie. Netso help 'n stem- en spraakterapeut mense wat sukkel om te praat of hul stem te gebruik, en put uit presies die stemtegnieke wat jy die hele jaar geoefen het. 'n Bewegingsterapeut gebruik fisiese beweging -- baie soos die dans- en dramabewegingswerk wat jy gedoen het -- om mense se fisiese of emosionele welsyn te ondersteun. Buiten terapie, dryf dramavaardighede ook loopbane soos radio- en televisie-aanbieding, waar duidelike, boeiende stemaflewering en gehoorverbinding geweldig saak maak, en om 'n seremoniemeester te wees, wat 'n gebeurtenis laat vloei en 'n gehoor se aandag behou. Laastens verteenwoordig agente uitvoerders professioneel, en help hulle om werk te vind en te bestuur. Wat al hierdie loopbane verbind is dit: die vaardighede wat jy die hele jaar gebou het -- stemuitdrukking, beweging, karakterisering, selfvertroue voor ander -- is waardevol ver buite die verhoog self.

english_content.narration_script: This final term of music listening adds the last new idea to your vocabulary: timbre. Timbre is what makes two instruments playing the exact same note still sound completely different -- a violin and a trumpet can play an identical pitch, at an identical volume, and still sound nothing alike, because of their timbre, or tone colour. Learning to describe timbre -- is a sound warm or bright, rough or smooth, thin or rich? -- completes the listening vocabulary you've built all year: meter, tempo, dynamics, texture, and now timbre, together with the meaning, story, and lyrics of a piece. With this full toolkit, you'll create a graphic score of a piece of music you've listened to, just as you did last term -- translating everything you hear, including timbre, into a visual sound picture using shapes, lines, and colours. A bright, sharp-timbred trumpet solo might become jagged yellow lines; a warm, smooth cello passage might become soft, flowing purple curves. As you finish this final unit, take a moment to notice how far your listening has come across the whole year: from simply identifying whether music was fast or slow, you can now describe meter, tempo, dynamics, texture, timbre, story, and lyrics together -- genuinely detailed, confident musical listening.

afrikaans_content.narration_script: Hierdie laaste kwartaal van musiekluister voeg die laaste nuwe idee by jou woordeskat: klankkleur. Klankkleur is wat maak dat twee instrumente wat presies dieselfde noot speel steeds heeltemal anders klink -- 'n viool en 'n trompet kan 'n identiese toonhoogte, teen 'n identiese volume, speel en steeds glad nie soortgelyk klink nie, weens hul klankkleur, of toonkleur. Om klankkleur te leer beskryf -- is 'n klank warm of helder, grof of glad, dun of ryk? -- voltooi die luisterwoordeskat wat jy die hele jaar gebou het: metrum, tempo, dinamiek, tekstuur, en nou klankkleur, saam met die betekenis, storie, en lirieke van 'n stuk. Met hierdie volledige gereedskapstel sal jy 'n grafiese partituur skep van 'n musiekstuk waarna jy geluister het, net soos jy verlede kwartaal gedoen het -- en alles wat jy hoor, insluitend klankkleur, in 'n visuele klankprentjie vertaal met vorms, lyne, en kleure. 'n Helder, skerp-klankkleurige trompetsolo mag hortende geel lyne word; 'n warm, gladde tjellopassasie mag sagte, vloeiende pers krulle word. Terwyl jy hierdie finale eenheid voltooi, neem 'n oomblik om op te merk hoe ver jou luister regdeur die hele jaar gekom het: van bloot identifiseer of musiek vinnig of stadig was, kan jy nou metrum, tempo, dinamiek, tekstuur, klankkleur, storie, en lirieke saam beskryf -- werklik gedetailleerde, selfversekerde musiekluister.

english_content.narration_script: This final music unit brings together everything you've built across the whole year into one culminating creative act: writing your own original song. As always, breathing exercises support your singing, and your repertoire continues with folksongs, light music, and rounds -- alongside the National Anthem of South Africa. You'll keep accompanying songs with body percussion and instruments, and now specifically perform music directly from graphic scores, reading the visual sound pictures you and your classmates have created and turning them back into real sound -- proving that a graphic score genuinely works as a form of musical notation. African drumming and rhythmic or melodic improvisation on an ostinato continue too, alongside creating sound pictures from a story or poem. But the biggest achievement of this term is writing your own four-line song -- both lyrics and melody -- based on a social issue that matters to you. This task pulls together everything from the whole year: the breathing and vocal skills to actually sing it, the melodic and rhythmic thinking to compose it, and something new -- using music as a genuine form of expression and even activism, saying something real about the world through a song entirely of your own making.

topic_name: Create in 3D: metamorphosis of a recyclable object

source_trace: Formal assessment project. Design: experiments with art elements and design principles in metamorphosis of a common recyclable object. Craft skills: pasting, cutting, modelling, wrapping, tying, stitc
lesson_metadata.source_section: Page 73, Grade 7 Term 4 Visual Arts Topic 2 (detailed content, not the page overview table)

learning_objectives: Design a 'metamorphosis' of a common recyclable object using art elements and design principles.
Apply craft skills (pasting, cutting, modelling, wrapping, tying, stitching, joining, scoring) to transform the object.
Explain how using recyclable materials connects this project to environmental awareness.

english_content.narration_script: This final visual arts unit of the year asks you to genuinely transform a common recyclable object -- a plastic bottle, a cardboard box, an old container -- into something completely different through 'metamorphosis,' a word that literally means a dramatic change in form. This is a formal assessment project, bringing together design thinking and hands-on craft skill. You'll experiment with art elements and design principles to plan how the object's original shape, texture, and material can become part of a new design, rather than being hidden or discarded. Achieving this metamorphosis requires real craft skill: pasting, cutting, modelling, wrapping, tying, stitching, joining, and scoring (creating a controlled fold line) are the physical techniques that let you reshape and reassemble materials with precision, not just glue things together randomly. Spatial awareness matters enormously here too -- you're not drawing an object anymore, you're physically constructing one, and you need to consciously think about how shapes fit together in real, three-dimensional space as you build. Underlying the whole project is a genuine concern for the environment: using recyclable materials isn't just a budget-friendly choice, it's a deliberate statement that everyday waste can become something valuable and creative, rather than simply being thrown away. As with all practical work, using your tools safely, being considerate of others, and sharing resources responsibly remain essential throughout.

afrikaans_content.narration_script: Hierdie finale visuelekuns-eenheid van die jaar vra jou om 'n algemene herwinbare voorwerp -- 'n plastiekbottel, 'n kartondoos, 'n ou houer -- werklik in iets heeltemal anders te verander deur 'metamorfose,' 'n woord wat letterlik 'n dramatiese verandering in vorm beteken. Dit is 'n formele assesseringsprojek, wat ontwerpdenke en praktiese vakmanskapvaardigheid saambring. Jy sal met kunselemente en ontwerpbeginsels eksperimenteer om te beplan hoe die voorwerp se oorspronklike vorm, tekstuur, en materiaal deel van 'n nuwe ontwerp kan word, eerder as om weggesteek of weggegooi te word. Om hierdie metamorfose te bereik verg werklike vakmanskapvaardigheid: plak, sny, modelleer, toedraai, vasbind, stik, verbind, en kartel (om 'n beheerde vouliniete skep) is die fisiese tegnieke wat jou toelaat om materiale met presisie te hervorm en te hersaamgestel, nie net lukraak dinge aanmekaar te plak nie. Ruimtelike bewustheid maak hier geweldig saak ook -- jy teken nie meer 'n voorwerp nie, jy bou fisies een, en jy moet bewustelik dink oor hoe vorms saam in werklike, driedimensionele ruimte pas terwyl jy bou. Onderliggend aan die hele projek is 'n ware besorgdheid vir die omgewing: om herwinbare materiale te gebruik is nie net 'n begrotingsvriendelike keuse nie, dit is 'n doelbewuste stelling dat alledaagse afval iets waardevols en kreatiefs kan word, eerder as om bloot weggegooi te word. Soos met alle praktiese werk, bly om jou gereedskap veilig te gebruik, ander in ag te neem, en hulpbronne verantwoordelik te deel noodsaaklik regdeur.

worked_example.problem: A learner uses a plastic bottle's curved shape as the base for a new flower sculpture, keeping its curve visible in the final design. What design approach does this reflect?
worked_example.problem_af: 'n Leerder gebruik 'n plastiekbottel se geboë vorm as die basis vir 'n nuwe blomskulptuur, en hou sy kurwe sigbaar in die finale ontwerp. Watter ontwerpbenadering weerspieël dit?
solution_steps: The object's original shape is being incorporated into the new design, not hidden.
This reflects the idea of metamorphosis -- transforming the object while its original form still informs the result.
worked_example.final_answer: It reflects metamorphosis -- transforming the object while letting its original shape inform the new design, rather than hiding it.

practice_questions.correct_answer: A dramatic change in form -- transforming a recyclable object into something completely different.
